Seasonal rainfall outlook

Research reconstruction · not an official forecast

Observations: CHIRPS v3.0 since 11 October 2026. Every cycle is calibrated and verified with CHIRPS v3.0. The 2026 forecasts shown here were recalibrated with v3.0 after their outcomes were known, so they are retrospective reconstructions, not forecasts issued in advance. The versions calibrated with CHIRPS v2.0 are in the release archive (release 2026-10-10.2); the v2.0 vs v3.0 comparison is in the Methods section.

Maps

Open full-size Download PNG

How to read this map

Grey, white and blank areas

Light grey: outside the selected area. Dark grey: inside the area but without values, for example cells where reference-period rainfall is too small for tercile categories, or (percent maps) below 10 mm. White on tercile maps: no category reaches 40%, or two categories tie. Sea cells have no CHIRPS data.

Smoothing and resolution. Maps are drawn on a 12× finer display grid with light Gaussian smoothing (σ = 0.6 grid cells); all numbers on this page use the original 0.25° grid. The model's own resolution is about 1°: each model cell covers 4×4 grid cells, so detail within a 1° box comes from local CHIRPS rainfall statistics used in the amount correction, not from the model.

Verification

Frozen forecasts compared with official CHIRPS v3.0 observations once a target period is complete. Each result is one season or month, so it shows what happened this time, not long-term reliability.

Historical performance

How forecasts made with the same method scored in past years against climatology (the observed frequency of each tercile in the training years, about one-third each). The main number is the cross-validated 1993–2016 score: each year is forecast with parameters fitted without that year. Later years are exploratory: they were seen while the method was chosen.

Bias correction

How the model’s rainfall amounts are corrected toward CHIRPS, and how alternative bias-correction methods compare with the operational one: the data, every method’s definition, the steps, the screening and confirmation results, and what they mean.

Each cycle has its own benchmark (initialization, season and months).

January initialization · FMAM and its months

Research benchmark. The published forecasts still use Mean-Variance Scaling (operational). This section compares 12 other rainfall-amount bias-correction methods with it, member by member, for every grid cell and target: a screening of the amount correction alone, then a confirmation through the full probability pipeline that also accounts for how a method is chosen.

Suggested method

The platform suggests a bias-correction method for every target and product from the historical evidence (the confirmation against CHIRPS, counting every method tried) and the independent validation seasons scored since (the shadow and validation runs), by a rule fixed before those seasons are scored. A suggestion is advice for a decision: the published forecast always uses Mean-Variance Scaling until a change is decided. 0 of 10 target–product combinations have a candidate.

The rule
  • Candidate: A method is a candidate only if the confirmation (CHIRPS, outer leave-one-year-out over the training years, full pipeline) finds it better than the operational method with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across every declared method and target, and not worse over the test years. Variants outside the declared family are not candidates.
  • Choice: Among candidates, the method the selection-aware procedure chooses from all training years (training-only information); if that method is not a candidate, the candidate with the best training-period score. Other candidates are listed as alternatives: a confirmation establishes improvement against the operational method, not a ranking among candidates.
  • Validation: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py). A candidate is 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the operational method, and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer seasons it stays a 'candidate'; with enough seasons and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'. Minimum: 3 seasons.

Summary — national aggregate (All Ethiopia)

  • All tested corrections improve national FMAM rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -0.696; corrected +0.009 to +0.029). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 0 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS.
  • Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are none, and the tercile (RPS) passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Feb, Mar), Power Transformation (Feb, Mar), Empirical Quantile Mapping (Feb) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Feb, Mar). Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Empirical Quantile Mapping Mar, Gamma Quantile Mapping Mar, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Feb, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Mar, Variance Scaling (unbounded) Feb and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Mar.

What the evidence supports

  • Published tercile probabilities: no tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling under this validation protocol (several have slightly higher point estimates); the selection-aware procedure is confirmed for none.
  • Rainfall amounts: no tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling under this validation protocol (several have slightly higher point estimates); the selection-aware procedure is confirmed for Feb.
  • The operational method stays Mean-Variance Scaling until a change is decided by initialization, target and product, and recorded in the docs, on this evidence; confirmed improvements limited to some months may justify a per-target choice.
  • If amounts and probabilities come to use different correction paths, the product metadata must record both methods so that every output can be traced.
  • The same screening and confirmation run for the other cycles with one configuration file each (config/bias_correction/).

Methods

Each method is fitted per grid cell and target from the training years only and applied to each member of the scored year. Methods that keep a “change signal” (DC, DQM, QDM, SDM, CDF-t) were designed for climate change, where a model’s reference period is compared with a future period; here the “future” is the forecast itself: the target year’s ensemble against the model climatology.

How overlapping names were resolved
  • Delta Change appeared twice in the requested list; it is one method.
  • Mean–Variance Scaling is the operational method, with the project’s 0.5–2 ratio limits. Variance Scaling uses the same algebra and the same fallback (ratio 1 where the model spread is below 1 mm) without the limits, so the comparison isolates the limits.
  • Delta Change returns the CHIRPS training years rescaled by the forecast signal (ensemble mean / model climatology): historical scenarios, not corrected members. Applied to each member instead it would be identical to Linear Scaling.
  • Square-root-space MVS (a mean–variance scaling of √x) is distinct from Power Transformation (a·xb with b fitted to the coefficient of variation).
  • The raw model is scored as a baseline, not screened.
Dry totals and tied values

A total at or below 1 mm in the month or season is “dry” (not a dry day). For the quantile-mapping methods (EQM, Gamma QM, DQM, QDM) the dry shares of the model climatology and of CHIRPS are estimated with the equal-year weights; a forecast’s dry members are spread evenly over the model’s dry probability by rank (deterministic stratified tie-breaking, with ties resolved by member index), and a probability within the CHIRPS dry share maps to 0 mm, also after any extrapolation of the upper tail. Without this, tied zeros share one probability and the corrected dry share does not follow CHIRPS. Tests cover repeated zeros, all-dry samples and very few wet values; the dry-month table under Results compares the shares. CDF-t, LOCI and the scaling methods have no occurrence adjustment; SDM uses its own rain-member rule (Switanek et al. 2017).

Steps

  1. 1

    Load

    Per-member totals of every target and year, and CHIRPS for 1993–2025.

    bias_benchmark.py · run_calibration.load_inputs
  2. 2

    Fit

    For each cell and target, the method’s statistics from the training years only, with equal-year weights.

    bias_methods.METHODS[key].fit
  3. 3

    Apply

    Correct every member of the scored year individually (member-wise).

    bias_methods.METHODS[key].apply
  4. 4

    Score

    Ensemble CRPS (and fair CRPS), ensemble-mean errors, spread–error, rank histograms, tercile RPS, dry shares and distribution ratios, per cell; then area-weighted per year.

    bias_benchmark.score_cells · summarise
  5. 5

    Screen

    Each method against Mean-Variance Scaling per target: one-sided sign-flip test on whole years, Holm within the method and across all methods, no harm in 2017–2025.

    bias_benchmark.make_gates
  6. 6

    Confirm

    Every method through the full probability pipeline (blend weight fitted inside the folds), and selection-aware procedures that choose the method each year from training-only scores.

    bias_confirmation.py

Scores
ScoreWhat it measuresReference
CRPS / CRPSSError of the corrected ensemble’s empirical distribution, as delivered, in mm; skill against the CHIRPS training climatology (the training years as an ensemble). Primary amount score.
Fair CRPS / CRPSSThe same under the interpretation that the members are a sample of an underlying distribution; reported as a diagnostic and screened separately. The justification assumes exchangeable members, which DC’s rescaled years and methods tied to the forecast mean or ranks only approximate.Ferro 2014
Ensemble meanBias, MAE, RMSE and correlation over years
Spread–error ratio√(mean ensemble variance·(K+1)/K) / RMSE of the ensemble mean; 1 = spread matches the error, < 1 too narrow
Rank histogram, reliability indexPosition of CHIRPS within the ensemble (10 bins; each rank interval shared among the bins it overlaps); index Σ|fi − 1/10|, 0 = flatDelle Monache et al. 2006
Tercile RPS / RPSS (screening)α = 0.5 smoothed member counts against the training CHIRPS terciles, without the blend: isolates the amount correction
Blended RPSS, Brier skill, reliability (confirmation)The published probability product: counts, smoothing and the climatology blend with its weight fitted inside the folds; category Brier skill for below and above normal; reliability tables
Dry shares and distribution ratiosPooled out-of-fold corrected members (equal-year weights) against CHIRPS of the same years: shares at exactly 0 mm and at ≤ 1 mm; mean, standard deviation, 10th and 90th percentile ratios (area-weighted medians)

Screening statistics for every method, target and score (within-method and family-wide Holm)

Screening rule (docs/36 rule applied as a screen): a method passes for a target and score if, on the leave-one-year-out 1993-2016 per-year scores, its mean improvement over mvs has a one-sided sign-flip p-value below 0.05 after Holm adjustment, and its mean score over 2017-2025 (fits on 1993-2016) is not worse. 'screen_pass': Holm across the 5 targets of one method. 'screen_pass_family': Holm across every method and target of the benchmark for that score. A screening pass is not an operational adoption decision (see the confirmation run).

Where the amount differences come from: cells grouped by their training-year climate

Each cell is grouped by its CHIRPS totals in the fold’s training years only: every year exactly 0 mm; every year ≤ 1 mm (not all 0); some years dry and some wet; never dry. Contributions are area-weighted CRPS differences from Mean-Variance Scaling (mm; negative favours the method) and add up to the national difference. Leave-one-year-out 1993–2016, All Ethiopia.

Confirmation: full pipeline and method selection

The screening isolates the amount correction. The confirmation evaluates what the site publishes: each method’s corrected members go through the full probability pipeline (tercile counts, smoothing and the climatology blend), with every fit and the blend weight inside the cross-validation folds. Two selection-aware procedures then choose a method for each left-out year using only the other training years — SEL-P by the lowest inner blended RPS (probabilities), SEL-A by the lowest inner CRPS (amounts) — so their scores include the effect of choosing among the 14 declared methods. ✓ = better than Mean-Variance Scaling with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 (methods: across all methods and targets; SEL-P/SEL-A: across the targets) and not worse over 2017–2025. Scope: All Ethiopia.

MVS ratio-limit study

The operational correction limits the spread ratio r = σobs/σmodel to 0.5–2. This study runs the same screening and confirmation for that correction with wider limits (1/3–3, 1/4–4) and none, all with the same fallback (r = 1 where the model spread is below 1 mm), to see whether the limits are worth changing. ✓ = better than the operational limits with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across the 3 alternatives × 5 targets and not worse over the test years. Run at commit fb7425f.

Confirmed better than the operational limits — published (blended) probabilities: none; rainfall amounts: MVS, ratio limits 1/3-3 (Feb), MVS, ratio limits 1/4-4 (Feb, Mar) and Variance Scaling (unbounded) (Feb, Mar).

Interpretation — national aggregate (All Ethiopia)

  1. All tested corrections improve national FMAM rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -0.696; corrected +0.009 to +0.029). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 0 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS.
  2. Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are none, and the tercile (RPS) passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Feb, Mar), Power Transformation (Feb, Mar), Empirical Quantile Mapping (Feb) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Feb, Mar). Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Empirical Quantile Mapping Mar, Gamma Quantile Mapping Mar, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Feb, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Mar, Variance Scaling (unbounded) Feb and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Mar.
  3. Empirical Quantile Mapping reproduces the CHIRPS distribution and, with the dry policy, its dry share (totals ≤ 1 mm: Feb 13.0% vs CHIRPS 12.9%); it passes the screening for Feb and Mar, but its FMAM amount skill is lower than Mean-Variance Scaling (+0.011 vs +0.025). A possible explanation is sampling noise in an empirical quantile function built from 23 CHIRPS values per fold; the results do not isolate it.
  4. Scaled Distribution Mapping follows the published algorithm (Switanek et al. 2017, steps 1–7; checked numerically against an independent implementation of the steps). Where the model is drier than CHIRPS it cannot add rain: in Feb 51% of model members exceed 1 mm against 87% of CHIRPS years, and SDM, by design, keeps the model’s number of rain members, so its corrected dry share is 50% (CHIRPS 13%).
  5. Delta Change has a high FMAM CRPSS in 1993–2016 (+0.029) but the gain does not pass the screening (Holm p = 1.00), it is lower in 2017–2025 (+0.010 vs +0.016), its ensemble is too wide (spread–error 1.04) and its tercile skill is low. It is the CHIRPS climatology rescaled by the forecast’s mean: historical scenarios, not corrected members.
  6. The methods that use the forecast’s own distribution (Detrended Quantile Mapping, Quantile Delta Mapping, Scaled Distribution Mapping, CDF-transform) score lower on FMAM terciles (+0.019 to +0.024 vs +0.034) and none passes the season screening. A possible explanation is that the distribution of a single forecast’s 25–51 members is a noisy estimate of the “future” distribution these methods were designed for; the results do not isolate the cause. Where model quantiles are dry, QDM falls back to the CHIRPS quantile (members affected: Feb 49% and Mar 20%), so its quantile changes are only partly preserved.
  7. May remains hard: every method has negative amount skill over 2017–2025.
  8. No tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling for the published tercile probabilities under this validation protocol, although several have slightly higher point estimates. Choosing the method each year from training-only scores, the probability procedure (SEL-P) scores FMAM blended RPSS +0.035 against +0.032, confirmed for none. Amounts: the amount procedure (SEL-A) scores CRPSS +0.020 against +0.025, confirmed for Feb; fixed methods confirmed against the family of all declared methods and targets: none.
  9. The climatology blend narrows the differences. Across the methods, FMAM RPSS (1993–2016) spans 0.014 after the blend against 0.016 for the unblended screening counts. A better amount correction is trusted more by the blend: in Feb the fitted weight on climatology is 0.35 with Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling against 0.73 with Mean-Variance Scaling.
  10. Choosing by training scores can backfire. For FMAM, SEL-A chose Delta Change from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean CRPS (Δ +0.345 mm, 95% interval -0.929 to +1.631 mm; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 5 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2020 and 2021); for Feb, SEL-P chose CDF-transform from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.020, 95% interval -0.013 to +0.052; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 3 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2021 and 2018); for Apr, SEL-P chose Local Intensity Scaling from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.001, 95% interval -0.001 to +0.004; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 5 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2020 and 2021); for May, SEL-P chose Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.007, 95% interval -0.004 to +0.020; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 3 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2021 and 2020); for FMAM, SEL-P chose Local Intensity Scaling from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.001, 95% interval -0.006 to +0.005; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 2 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2021 and 2018). These choices fail the no-harm rule; where the interval includes 0 they do not establish a significant deterioration. A method that ranks first on the training years is not, on that alone, a replacement.
  11. No cell of All Ethiopia has exactly 0 mm in every training year, for any target, at 0.25° with CHIRPS. The all-zero guard (a separate MVS variant, outside the declared family) therefore never acts and equals Mean-Variance Scaling: the non-zero totals that Mean-Variance Scaling gives where every training year is 0 mm (its spread ratio cannot fall below 0.5) do not arise in these data. The guard remains a documented option; a finite history of zero rainfall does not make rain impossible.

3 of the 14 interpretation statements do not hold for this cycle’s results and are not shown (each is checked against the numbers before it is displayed).

Caveats
  • Screening skill is from 1993–2016 leave-one-year-out (clean) and 2017–2025 (exploratory: these years were seen while the operational method was chosen).
  • Screening tercile scores use smoothed member counts without the climatology blend; the confirmation scores the blended product.
  • Two multiplicity families are shown: within one method across its targets (✓) and across all methods and targets (✓✓). The confirmation’s selection-aware procedures include the method choice in the evaluation itself.
  • Scores are area-weighted over many correlated cells but tested year by year, so each year counts once.
  • The ordinary CRPS scores the delivered ensemble; the fair CRPS is a diagnostic under a sampling interpretation that DC’s rescaled years and methods tied to the forecast mean or ranks only approximate.
  • Results are national aggregates unless a table says otherwise; a method can rank differently in a region (switch the tables to the regional view).

February initialization · FMAM and its months

Research benchmark. The published forecasts still use Mean-Variance Scaling (operational). This section compares 12 other rainfall-amount bias-correction methods with it, member by member, for every grid cell and target: a screening of the amount correction alone, then a confirmation through the full probability pipeline that also accounts for how a method is chosen.

Suggested method

The platform suggests a bias-correction method for every target and product from the historical evidence (the confirmation against CHIRPS, counting every method tried) and the independent validation seasons scored since (the shadow and validation runs), by a rule fixed before those seasons are scored. A suggestion is advice for a decision: the published forecast always uses Mean-Variance Scaling until a change is decided. 1 of 10 target–product combinations have a candidate.

The rule
  • Candidate: A method is a candidate only if the confirmation (CHIRPS, outer leave-one-year-out over the training years, full pipeline) finds it better than the operational method with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across every declared method and target, and not worse over the test years. Variants outside the declared family are not candidates.
  • Choice: Among candidates, the method the selection-aware procedure chooses from all training years (training-only information); if that method is not a candidate, the candidate with the best training-period score. Other candidates are listed as alternatives: a confirmation establishes improvement against the operational method, not a ranking among candidates.
  • Validation: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py). A candidate is 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the operational method, and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer seasons it stays a 'candidate'; with enough seasons and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'. Minimum: 3 seasons.

Summary — national aggregate (All Ethiopia)

  • All tested corrections improve national FMAM rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -0.585; corrected -0.059 to -0.005). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 0 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS.
  • Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are none, and the tercile (RPS) passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Feb, Mar), Power Transformation (Feb, Mar) and Empirical Quantile Mapping (Feb). Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Empirical Quantile Mapping Mar, Gamma Quantile Mapping Feb, Gamma Quantile Mapping Mar, Power Transformation May, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Feb, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Mar and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Feb.

What the evidence supports

  • Published tercile probabilities: confirmed against Mean-Variance Scaling (family-wide, full pipeline): Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling for Feb. The selection-aware procedure is confirmed for Feb.
  • Rainfall amounts: no tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling under this validation protocol (several have slightly higher point estimates); the selection-aware procedure is confirmed for Feb and Mar.
  • The operational method stays Mean-Variance Scaling until a change is decided by initialization, target and product, and recorded in the docs, on this evidence; confirmed improvements limited to some months may justify a per-target choice.
  • If amounts and probabilities come to use different correction paths, the product metadata must record both methods so that every output can be traced.
  • The same screening and confirmation run for the other cycles with one configuration file each (config/bias_correction/).

Methods

Each method is fitted per grid cell and target from the training years only and applied to each member of the scored year. Methods that keep a “change signal” (DC, DQM, QDM, SDM, CDF-t) were designed for climate change, where a model’s reference period is compared with a future period; here the “future” is the forecast itself: the target year’s ensemble against the model climatology.

How overlapping names were resolved
  • Delta Change appeared twice in the requested list; it is one method.
  • Mean–Variance Scaling is the operational method, with the project’s 0.5–2 ratio limits. Variance Scaling uses the same algebra and the same fallback (ratio 1 where the model spread is below 1 mm) without the limits, so the comparison isolates the limits.
  • Delta Change returns the CHIRPS training years rescaled by the forecast signal (ensemble mean / model climatology): historical scenarios, not corrected members. Applied to each member instead it would be identical to Linear Scaling.
  • Square-root-space MVS (a mean–variance scaling of √x) is distinct from Power Transformation (a·xb with b fitted to the coefficient of variation).
  • The raw model is scored as a baseline, not screened.
Dry totals and tied values

A total at or below 1 mm in the month or season is “dry” (not a dry day). For the quantile-mapping methods (EQM, Gamma QM, DQM, QDM) the dry shares of the model climatology and of CHIRPS are estimated with the equal-year weights; a forecast’s dry members are spread evenly over the model’s dry probability by rank (deterministic stratified tie-breaking, with ties resolved by member index), and a probability within the CHIRPS dry share maps to 0 mm, also after any extrapolation of the upper tail. Without this, tied zeros share one probability and the corrected dry share does not follow CHIRPS. Tests cover repeated zeros, all-dry samples and very few wet values; the dry-month table under Results compares the shares. CDF-t, LOCI and the scaling methods have no occurrence adjustment; SDM uses its own rain-member rule (Switanek et al. 2017).

Steps

  1. 1

    Load

    Per-member totals of every target and year, and CHIRPS for 1993–2025.

    bias_benchmark.py · run_calibration.load_inputs
  2. 2

    Fit

    For each cell and target, the method’s statistics from the training years only, with equal-year weights.

    bias_methods.METHODS[key].fit
  3. 3

    Apply

    Correct every member of the scored year individually (member-wise).

    bias_methods.METHODS[key].apply
  4. 4

    Score

    Ensemble CRPS (and fair CRPS), ensemble-mean errors, spread–error, rank histograms, tercile RPS, dry shares and distribution ratios, per cell; then area-weighted per year.

    bias_benchmark.score_cells · summarise
  5. 5

    Screen

    Each method against Mean-Variance Scaling per target: one-sided sign-flip test on whole years, Holm within the method and across all methods, no harm in 2017–2025.

    bias_benchmark.make_gates
  6. 6

    Confirm

    Every method through the full probability pipeline (blend weight fitted inside the folds), and selection-aware procedures that choose the method each year from training-only scores.

    bias_confirmation.py

Scores
ScoreWhat it measuresReference
CRPS / CRPSSError of the corrected ensemble’s empirical distribution, as delivered, in mm; skill against the CHIRPS training climatology (the training years as an ensemble). Primary amount score.
Fair CRPS / CRPSSThe same under the interpretation that the members are a sample of an underlying distribution; reported as a diagnostic and screened separately. The justification assumes exchangeable members, which DC’s rescaled years and methods tied to the forecast mean or ranks only approximate.Ferro 2014
Ensemble meanBias, MAE, RMSE and correlation over years
Spread–error ratio√(mean ensemble variance·(K+1)/K) / RMSE of the ensemble mean; 1 = spread matches the error, < 1 too narrow
Rank histogram, reliability indexPosition of CHIRPS within the ensemble (10 bins; each rank interval shared among the bins it overlaps); index Σ|fi − 1/10|, 0 = flatDelle Monache et al. 2006
Tercile RPS / RPSS (screening)α = 0.5 smoothed member counts against the training CHIRPS terciles, without the blend: isolates the amount correction
Blended RPSS, Brier skill, reliability (confirmation)The published probability product: counts, smoothing and the climatology blend with its weight fitted inside the folds; category Brier skill for below and above normal; reliability tables
Dry shares and distribution ratiosPooled out-of-fold corrected members (equal-year weights) against CHIRPS of the same years: shares at exactly 0 mm and at ≤ 1 mm; mean, standard deviation, 10th and 90th percentile ratios (area-weighted medians)

Screening statistics for every method, target and score (within-method and family-wide Holm)

Screening rule (docs/36 rule applied as a screen): a method passes for a target and score if, on the leave-one-year-out 1993-2016 per-year scores, its mean improvement over mvs has a one-sided sign-flip p-value below 0.05 after Holm adjustment, and its mean score over 2017-2025 (fits on 1993-2016) is not worse. 'screen_pass': Holm across the 5 targets of one method. 'screen_pass_family': Holm across every method and target of the benchmark for that score. A screening pass is not an operational adoption decision (see the confirmation run).

Where the amount differences come from: cells grouped by their training-year climate

Each cell is grouped by its CHIRPS totals in the fold’s training years only: every year exactly 0 mm; every year ≤ 1 mm (not all 0); some years dry and some wet; never dry. Contributions are area-weighted CRPS differences from Mean-Variance Scaling (mm; negative favours the method) and add up to the national difference. Leave-one-year-out 1993–2016, All Ethiopia.

Confirmation: full pipeline and method selection

The screening isolates the amount correction. The confirmation evaluates what the site publishes: each method’s corrected members go through the full probability pipeline (tercile counts, smoothing and the climatology blend), with every fit and the blend weight inside the cross-validation folds. Two selection-aware procedures then choose a method for each left-out year using only the other training years — SEL-P by the lowest inner blended RPS (probabilities), SEL-A by the lowest inner CRPS (amounts) — so their scores include the effect of choosing among the 14 declared methods. ✓ = better than Mean-Variance Scaling with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 (methods: across all methods and targets; SEL-P/SEL-A: across the targets) and not worse over 2017–2025. Scope: All Ethiopia.

The operational correction limits the spread ratio r = σobs/σmodel to 0.5–2. This study runs the same screening and confirmation for that correction with wider limits (1/3–3, 1/4–4) and none, all with the same fallback (r = 1 where the model spread is below 1 mm), to see whether the limits are worth changing. ✓ = better than the operational limits with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across the 3 alternatives × 5 targets and not worse over the test years. Run at commit fb7425f.

Confirmed better than the operational limits — published (blended) probabilities: none; rainfall amounts: none.

Interpretation — national aggregate (All Ethiopia)

  1. All tested corrections improve national FMAM rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -0.585; corrected -0.059 to -0.005). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 0 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS.
  2. Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are none, and the tercile (RPS) passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Feb, Mar), Power Transformation (Feb, Mar) and Empirical Quantile Mapping (Feb). Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Empirical Quantile Mapping Mar, Gamma Quantile Mapping Feb, Gamma Quantile Mapping Mar, Power Transformation May, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Feb, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Mar and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Feb.
  3. Empirical Quantile Mapping reproduces the CHIRPS distribution and, with the dry policy, its dry share (totals ≤ 1 mm: Feb 12.9% vs CHIRPS 12.9%); it passes the screening for Feb and Mar, but its FMAM amount skill is lower than Mean-Variance Scaling (-0.018 vs -0.007). A possible explanation is sampling noise in an empirical quantile function built from 23 CHIRPS values per fold; the results do not isolate it.
  4. Scaled Distribution Mapping follows the published algorithm (Switanek et al. 2017, steps 1–7; checked numerically against an independent implementation of the steps). Where the model is drier than CHIRPS it cannot add rain: in Feb 58% of model members exceed 1 mm against 87% of CHIRPS years, and SDM, by design, keeps the model’s number of rain members, so its corrected dry share is 44% (CHIRPS 13%).
  5. The methods that use the forecast’s own distribution (Detrended Quantile Mapping, Quantile Delta Mapping, Scaled Distribution Mapping, CDF-transform) score lower on FMAM terciles (-0.045 to -0.023 vs +0.005) and none passes the season screening. A possible explanation is that the distribution of a single forecast’s 25–51 members is a noisy estimate of the “future” distribution these methods were designed for; the results do not isolate the cause. Where model quantiles are dry, QDM falls back to the CHIRPS quantile (members affected: Feb 42% and Mar 18%), so its quantile changes are only partly preserved.
  6. Published probabilities: confirmed better than Mean-Variance Scaling: Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Feb). Choosing the method each year from training-only scores, the probability procedure (SEL-P) scores FMAM blended RPSS +0.020 against +0.021, confirmed for Feb. Amounts: the amount procedure (SEL-A) scores CRPSS -0.011 against -0.007, confirmed for Feb and Mar; fixed methods confirmed against the family of all declared methods and targets: none.
  7. The climatology blend narrows the differences. Across the methods, FMAM RPSS (1993–2016) spans 0.010 after the blend against 0.051 for the unblended screening counts. A better amount correction is trusted more by the blend: in Mar the fitted weight on climatology is 0.47 with Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling against 0.71 with Mean-Variance Scaling.
  8. Choosing by training scores can backfire. For Apr, SEL-P chose Linear Scaling from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.000, 95% interval -0.004 to +0.004; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 4 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2021 and 2020); for May, SEL-P chose Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.001, 95% interval -0.006 to +0.009; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 5 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2021 and 2025). These choices fail the no-harm rule; where the interval includes 0 they do not establish a significant deterioration. A method that ranks first on the training years is not, on that alone, a replacement.
  9. No cell of All Ethiopia has exactly 0 mm in every training year, for any target, at 0.25° with CHIRPS. The all-zero guard (a separate MVS variant, outside the declared family) therefore never acts and equals Mean-Variance Scaling: the non-zero totals that Mean-Variance Scaling gives where every training year is 0 mm (its spread ratio cannot fall below 0.5) do not arise in these data. The guard remains a documented option; a finite history of zero rainfall does not make rain impossible.

5 of the 14 interpretation statements do not hold for this cycle’s results and are not shown (each is checked against the numbers before it is displayed).

Caveats
  • Screening skill is from 1993–2016 leave-one-year-out (clean) and 2017–2025 (exploratory: these years were seen while the operational method was chosen).
  • Screening tercile scores use smoothed member counts without the climatology blend; the confirmation scores the blended product.
  • Two multiplicity families are shown: within one method across its targets (✓) and across all methods and targets (✓✓). The confirmation’s selection-aware procedures include the method choice in the evaluation itself.
  • Scores are area-weighted over many correlated cells but tested year by year, so each year counts once.
  • The ordinary CRPS scores the delivered ensemble; the fair CRPS is a diagnostic under a sampling interpretation that DC’s rescaled years and methods tied to the forecast mean or ranks only approximate.
  • Results are national aggregates unless a table says otherwise; a method can rank differently in a region (switch the tables to the regional view).

May initialization · JJAS and its months

Research benchmark. The published forecasts still use Mean-Variance Scaling (operational). This section compares 12 other rainfall-amount bias-correction methods with it, member by member, for every grid cell and target: a screening of the amount correction alone, then a confirmation through the full probability pipeline that also accounts for how a method is chosen.

Suggested method

The platform suggests a bias-correction method for every target and product from the historical evidence (the confirmation against CHIRPS, counting every method tried) and the independent validation seasons scored since (the shadow and validation runs), by a rule fixed before those seasons are scored. A suggestion is advice for a decision: the published forecast always uses Mean-Variance Scaling until a change is decided. 2 of 10 target–product combinations have a candidate.

The rule
  • Candidate: A method is a candidate only if the confirmation (CHIRPS, outer leave-one-year-out over the training years, full pipeline) finds it better than the operational method with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across every declared method and target, and not worse over the test years. Variants outside the declared family are not candidates.
  • Choice: Among candidates, the method the selection-aware procedure chooses from all training years (training-only information); if that method is not a candidate, the candidate with the best training-period score. Other candidates are listed as alternatives: a confirmation establishes improvement against the operational method, not a ranking among candidates.
  • Validation: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py). A candidate is 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the operational method, and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer seasons it stays a 'candidate'; with enough seasons and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'. Minimum: 3 seasons.

Summary — national aggregate (All Ethiopia)

  • All tested corrections improve national JJAS rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -1.311; corrected -0.078 to -0.025). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 0 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS.
  • Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are Variance Scaling (unbounded) (Jul, Aug), Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Aug), Power Transformation (Aug) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Aug), and the tercile (RPS) passes are none. Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Gamma Quantile Mapping Jun, Gamma Quantile Mapping Sep, Power Transformation Jul, Power Transformation Jun, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling JJAS, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Jul, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Jun, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Sep and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Sep.

What the evidence supports

  • Published tercile probabilities: no tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling under this validation protocol (several have slightly higher point estimates); the selection-aware procedure is confirmed for none.
  • Rainfall amounts: confirmed against Mean-Variance Scaling (family-wide, full pipeline): Variance Scaling (unbounded) for Jul and Aug; Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling for Aug; Power Transformation for Aug; Gamma Quantile Mapping for Aug. The selection-aware procedure is confirmed for Jun, Aug and Sep. These comparisons establish improvement against the reference, not that one candidate is better than another.
  • The operational method stays Mean-Variance Scaling until a change is decided by initialization, target and product, and recorded in the docs, on this evidence; confirmed improvements limited to some months may justify a per-target choice.
  • If amounts and probabilities come to use different correction paths, the product metadata must record both methods so that every output can be traced.
  • The same screening and confirmation run for the other cycles with one configuration file each (config/bias_correction/).

Methods

Each method is fitted per grid cell and target from the training years only and applied to each member of the scored year. Methods that keep a “change signal” (DC, DQM, QDM, SDM, CDF-t) were designed for climate change, where a model’s reference period is compared with a future period; here the “future” is the forecast itself: the target year’s ensemble against the model climatology.

How overlapping names were resolved
  • Delta Change appeared twice in the requested list; it is one method.
  • Mean–Variance Scaling is the operational method, with the project’s 0.5–2 ratio limits. Variance Scaling uses the same algebra and the same fallback (ratio 1 where the model spread is below 1 mm) without the limits, so the comparison isolates the limits.
  • Delta Change returns the CHIRPS training years rescaled by the forecast signal (ensemble mean / model climatology): historical scenarios, not corrected members. Applied to each member instead it would be identical to Linear Scaling.
  • Square-root-space MVS (a mean–variance scaling of √x) is distinct from Power Transformation (a·xb with b fitted to the coefficient of variation).
  • The raw model is scored as a baseline, not screened.
Dry totals and tied values

A total at or below 1 mm in the month or season is “dry” (not a dry day). For the quantile-mapping methods (EQM, Gamma QM, DQM, QDM) the dry shares of the model climatology and of CHIRPS are estimated with the equal-year weights; a forecast’s dry members are spread evenly over the model’s dry probability by rank (deterministic stratified tie-breaking, with ties resolved by member index), and a probability within the CHIRPS dry share maps to 0 mm, also after any extrapolation of the upper tail. Without this, tied zeros share one probability and the corrected dry share does not follow CHIRPS. Tests cover repeated zeros, all-dry samples and very few wet values; the dry-month table under Results compares the shares. CDF-t, LOCI and the scaling methods have no occurrence adjustment; SDM uses its own rain-member rule (Switanek et al. 2017).

Mean-Variance Scaling (operational)
mvs		scalingx' = max(0, mu_obs + r (x - mu_model)), r = clip(sd_obs/sd_model, 0.5, 2); r = 1 if sd_model < 1 mmyesno{"ratio_bounds": [0.5, 2.0], "min_model_sd": 1.0}Torralba et al. 2017, Manzanas et al. 2019
Variance Scaling (unbounded)
vs		scalingSame algebra and the same r = 1 fallback (sd_model < 1 mm) as MVS, without the 0.5-2 ratio limitsyesno{"ratio_bounds": null, "min_model_sd": 1.0}Teutschbein & Seibert 2012
Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling
sqrt_mvs		scalingMVS applied to sqrt(x) (r limits 0.5-2; r = 1 if the sqrt-space sd < 0.1), clipped at 0 and squared back (docs/36)yesno{"ratio_bounds": [0.5, 2.0], "min_model_sd": 0.1, "space": "sqrt"}Manzanas et al. 2019
Power Transformation
pt		scalingx' = a x^b: b (0.1-3) matches the coefficient of variation where reachable (bound hits reported), a the meanyesno{"b_bounds": [0.1, 3.0]}Leander & Buishand 2007, Teutschbein & Seibert 2012
Delta Change
dc		change-preservingTraining-year CHIRPS totals times a = forecast ensemble mean / model mean (a in 0.2-5): historical scenarios, not corrected membersno (one value per training year)yes{"ratio_bounds": [0.2, 5.0], "min_model_mean": 0.1}Hay et al. 2000, Teutschbein & Seibert 2012
Local Intensity Scaling
loci		scalingModel threshold with the observed frequency of totals above 1 mm, then intensity scaling above it (designed for daily rainfall; here monthly or seasonal totals)yesno{"wet_threshold": 1.0}Schmidli et al. 2006
Empirical Quantile Mapping
eqm		quantile mappingx' = Q_obs(F_model(x)) with the dry policy; constant-ratio extrapolation outside the training rangeyesno{"extrapolation": "constant_ratio", "wet_threshold": 1.0}Boé et al. 2007, Themeßl et al. 2011, Gudmundsson et al. 2012
Gamma Quantile Mapping
gqm		quantile mappingx' = G_obs^-1(G_model(x)), G = dry mass (<= 1 mm) + gamma by weighted maximum likelihood, with the dry policy; linear scaling where fewer than 3 wet valuesyesno{"wet_threshold": 1.0}Piani et al. 2010
Detrended Quantile Mapping
dqm		change-preservinga * EQM(x / a), a = forecast ensemble mean / model mean (0.2-5): removes and reapplies the bounded ratio; exact preservation of the final mean anomaly is not guaranteedyesyes{"extrapolation": "constant_ratio", "ratio_bounds": [0.2, 5.0], "min_model_mean": 0.1, "wet_threshold": 1.0}Cannon et al. 2015
Quantile Delta Mapping
qdm		change-preservingx' = Q_obs(tau) * x / Q_model(tau), tau = rank of x in the forecast ensemble; change capped at 5 and replaced by Q_obs(tau) where Q_model(tau) <= 1 mm (both reported), so preservation is partial thereyesyes{"max_ratio": 5.0, "wet_threshold": 1.0}Cannon et al. 2015
Scaled Distribution Mapping
sdm		change-preservingSwitanek et al. (2017) precipitation steps 1-7: gamma fits, recurrence intervals interpolated to the forecast's length, scaled CDF, rain-member count; model climatology with equal-year weightsyesyes{"wet_threshold": 1.0}Switanek et al. 2017
CDF-transform
cdft		change-preservingF_obs,f = F_obs(F_model^-1(F_forecast)); x' = F_obs,f^-1(F_forecast(x)); implementation choices: model and forecast first scaled to the CHIRPS mean, values stay within the scaled forecast rangeyesyes{"min_model_mean": 0.1}Michelangeli et al. 2009, Vrac et al. 2012
MVS with all-zero guard (variant)
mvs_zero_guard		variantOperational MVS, but corrected totals are 0 mm where every training year has exactly 0 mm (a documented modelling choice, not a physical rule)yesno{"ratio_bounds": [0.5, 2.0], "min_model_sd": 1.0, "zero_guard": true}Torralba et al. 2017, Manzanas et al. 2019

Steps

  1. 1

    Load

    Per-member totals of every target and year, and CHIRPS for 1993–2025.

    bias_benchmark.py · run_calibration.load_inputs
  2. 2

    Fit

    For each cell and target, the method’s statistics from the training years only, with equal-year weights.

    bias_methods.METHODS[key].fit
  3. 3

    Apply

    Correct every member of the scored year individually (member-wise).

    bias_methods.METHODS[key].apply
  4. 4

    Score

    Ensemble CRPS (and fair CRPS), ensemble-mean errors, spread–error, rank histograms, tercile RPS, dry shares and distribution ratios, per cell; then area-weighted per year.

    bias_benchmark.score_cells · summarise
  5. 5

    Screen

    Each method against Mean-Variance Scaling per target: one-sided sign-flip test on whole years, Holm within the method and across all methods, no harm in 2017–2025.

    bias_benchmark.make_gates
  6. 6

    Confirm

    Every method through the full probability pipeline (blend weight fitted inside the folds), and selection-aware procedures that choose the method each year from training-only scores.

    bias_confirmation.py
Evaluation designs (no amount method has a parameter tuned on scores)
DesignFitsScoredRole
Screening: trainingleave-one-year-out within 1993–2016each 1993–2016 yearclean evidence for the screening
Screening: test1993–20162017–2025exploratory (these years were seen before)
Screening: fullleave-one-year-out within 1993–2025each yearper-cell maps and distribution checks (descriptive)
Confirmationouter leave-one-year-out within 1993–2016; inside each fold the blend weight (inner leave-one-year-out) and, for SEL-P/SEL-A, the method choiceeach 1993–2016 yearfull pipeline; accounts for the method choice
Confirmation: test1993–2016 (fits, blend weight and method choice)2017–2025exploratory
Forecast1993–20252026 membersmember-by-member comparison
Scores
ScoreWhat it measuresReference
CRPS / CRPSSError of the corrected ensemble’s empirical distribution, as delivered, in mm; skill against the CHIRPS training climatology (the training years as an ensemble). Primary amount score.
Fair CRPS / CRPSSThe same under the interpretation that the members are a sample of an underlying distribution; reported as a diagnostic and screened separately. The justification assumes exchangeable members, which DC’s rescaled years and methods tied to the forecast mean or ranks only approximate.Ferro 2014
Ensemble meanBias, MAE, RMSE and correlation over years
Spread–error ratio√(mean ensemble variance·(K+1)/K) / RMSE of the ensemble mean; 1 = spread matches the error, < 1 too narrow
Rank histogram, reliability indexPosition of CHIRPS within the ensemble (10 bins; each rank interval shared among the bins it overlaps); index Σ|fi − 1/10|, 0 = flatDelle Monache et al. 2006
Tercile RPS / RPSS (screening)α = 0.5 smoothed member counts against the training CHIRPS terciles, without the blend: isolates the amount correction
Blended RPSS, Brier skill, reliability (confirmation)The published probability product: counts, smoothing and the climatology blend with its weight fitted inside the folds; category Brier skill for below and above normal; reliability tables
Dry shares and distribution ratiosPooled out-of-fold corrected members (equal-year weights) against CHIRPS of the same years: shares at exactly 0 mm and at ≤ 1 mm; mean, standard deviation, 10th and 90th percentile ratios (area-weighted medians)

Screening statistics for every method, target and score (within-method and family-wide Holm)

Screening rule (docs/36 rule applied as a screen): a method passes for a target and score if, on the leave-one-year-out 1993-2016 per-year scores, its mean improvement over mvs has a one-sided sign-flip p-value below 0.05 after Holm adjustment, and its mean score over 2017-2025 (fits on 1993-2016) is not worse. 'screen_pass': Holm across the 5 targets of one method. 'screen_pass_family': Holm across every method and target of the benchmark for that score. A screening pass is not an operational adoption decision (see the confirmation run).

Where the amount differences come from: cells grouped by their training-year climate

Each cell is grouped by its CHIRPS totals in the fold’s training years only: every year exactly 0 mm; every year ≤ 1 mm (not all 0); some years dry and some wet; never dry. Contributions are area-weighted CRPS differences from Mean-Variance Scaling (mm; negative favours the method) and add up to the national difference. Leave-one-year-out 1993–2016, All Ethiopia.

Confirmation: full pipeline and method selection

The screening isolates the amount correction. The confirmation evaluates what the site publishes: each method’s corrected members go through the full probability pipeline (tercile counts, smoothing and the climatology blend), with every fit and the blend weight inside the cross-validation folds. Two selection-aware procedures then choose a method for each left-out year using only the other training years — SEL-P by the lowest inner blended RPS (probabilities), SEL-A by the lowest inner CRPS (amounts) — so their scores include the effect of choosing among the 14 declared methods. ✓ = better than Mean-Variance Scaling with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 (methods: across all methods and targets; SEL-P/SEL-A: across the targets) and not worse over 2017–2025. MVS ratio-limit study

The operational correction limits the spread ratio r = σobs/σmodel to 0.5–2. This study runs the same screening and confirmation for that correction with wider limits (1/3–3, 1/4–4) and none, all with the same fallback (r = 1 where the model spread is below 1 mm), to see whether the limits are worth changing. ✓ = better than the operational limits with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across the 3 alternatives × 5 targets and not worse over the test years. Run at commit fb7425f.

Confirmed better than the operational limits — published (blended) probabilities: none; rainfall amounts: MVS, ratio limits 1/3-3 (Jul, Aug, Sep), MVS, ratio limits 1/4-4 (Jul, Aug, Sep) and Variance Scaling (unbounded) (Jul, Aug, Sep).

Open full size

Interpretation — national aggregate (All Ethiopia)

  1. All tested corrections improve national JJAS rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -1.311; corrected -0.078 to -0.025). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 0 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS.
  2. Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are Variance Scaling (unbounded) (Jul, Aug), Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Aug), Power Transformation (Aug) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Aug), and the tercile (RPS) passes are none. Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Gamma Quantile Mapping Jun, Gamma Quantile Mapping Sep, Power Transformation Jul, Power Transformation Jun, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling JJAS, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Jul, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Jun, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Sep and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Sep.
  3. Variance Scaling (unbounded) is at least as good as Mean-Variance Scaling in the national aggregate for every tested target and period, on amounts and unblended terciles (JJAS CRPSS -0.027 vs -0.028 in 1993–2016, -0.016 vs -0.018 in 2017–2025). Its JJAS amount screening pass does not survive the family-wide correction. Members clipped to 0 mm in the months: 1.3%–9.9% with Mean-Variance Scaling, 0.2%–1.4% with this method. This need not hold in each region; see the tables for the JJAS R1+R2 rainfall domain.
  4. Empirical Quantile Mapping reproduces the CHIRPS distribution and, with the dry policy, its dry share (totals ≤ 1 mm: —); it passes the screening for none, but its JJAS amount skill is lower than Mean-Variance Scaling (-0.040 vs -0.028). A possible explanation is sampling noise in an empirical quantile function built from 23 CHIRPS values per fold; the results do not isolate it.
  5. The methods that use the forecast’s own distribution (Detrended Quantile Mapping, Quantile Delta Mapping, Scaled Distribution Mapping, CDF-transform) score lower on JJAS terciles (-0.080 to -0.044 vs -0.017) and none passes the season screening. A possible explanation is that the distribution of a single forecast’s 25–51 members is a noisy estimate of the “future” distribution these methods were designed for; the results do not isolate the cause.
  6. Jun and Sep remain hard: every method has negative amount skill over 2017–2025.
  7. No tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling for the published tercile probabilities under this validation protocol, although several have slightly higher point estimates. Choosing the method each year from training-only scores, the probability procedure (SEL-P) scores JJAS blended RPSS +0.025 against +0.027, confirmed for none. Amounts: the amount procedure (SEL-A) scores CRPSS -0.036 against -0.028, confirmed for Jun, Aug and Sep; fixed methods confirmed against the family of all declared methods and targets: Variance Scaling (unbounded) (Jul, Aug), Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Aug), Power Transformation (Aug) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Aug).
  8. The climatology blend narrows the differences. Across the methods, JJAS RPSS (1993–2016) spans 0.010 after the blend against 0.066 for the unblended screening counts. A better amount correction is trusted more by the blend: in Jun the fitted weight on climatology is 0.75 with Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling against 0.80 with Mean-Variance Scaling.
  9. Choosing by training scores can backfire. For Jul, SEL-A chose Delta Change from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean CRPS (Δ +0.194 mm, 95% interval -0.094 to +0.517 mm; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 3 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2020 and 2024); for Sep, SEL-P chose Scaled Distribution Mapping from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.001, 95% interval -0.001 to +0.003; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 5 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2018 and 2024); for JJAS, SEL-P chose Delta Change from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.004, 95% interval -0.000 to +0.009; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 2 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2018 and 2023). These choices fail the no-harm rule; where the interval includes 0 they do not establish a significant deterioration. A method that ranks first on the training years is not, on that alone, a replacement.
  10. Where the confirmed amount gains come from (climate groups from each fold’s training years; contributions add up to the national difference from Mean-Variance Scaling): Variance Scaling (unbounded) in Jul (Δ CRPS -0.139 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.014 mm (10%; 4% of the area), mixed -0.042 mm (30%; 9% of the area), always wet -0.083 mm (60%; 88% of the area); Variance Scaling (unbounded) in Aug (Δ CRPS -0.129 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.008 mm (6%; 2% of the area), mixed -0.018 mm (14%; 3% of the area), always wet -0.103 mm (80%; 95% of the area); Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling in Aug (Δ CRPS -0.096 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.004 mm (5%; 2% of the area), mixed -0.012 mm (13%; 3% of the area), always wet -0.079 mm (83%; 95% of the area); Power Transformation in Aug (Δ CRPS -0.124 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.008 mm (6%; 2% of the area), mixed -0.017 mm (14%; 3% of the area), always wet -0.099 mm (80%; 95% of the area); Gamma Quantile Mapping in Aug (Δ CRPS -0.128 mm): all ≤ 1 mm +0.000 mm (-0%; 2% of the area), mixed -0.012 mm (9%; 3% of the area), always wet -0.116 mm (91%; 95% of the area).
  11. No cell of All Ethiopia has exactly 0 mm in every training year, for any target, at 0.25° with CHIRPS. The all-zero guard (a separate MVS variant, outside the declared family) therefore never acts and equals Mean-Variance Scaling: the non-zero totals that Mean-Variance Scaling gives where every training year is 0 mm (its spread ratio cannot fall below 0.5) do not arise in these data. The guard remains a documented option; a finite history of zero rainfall does not make rain impossible.

4 of the 15 interpretation statements do not hold for this cycle’s results and are not shown (each is checked against the numbers before it is displayed).

Caveats
  • Screening skill is from 1993–2016 leave-one-year-out (clean) and 2017–2025 (exploratory: these years were seen while the operational method was chosen).
  • Screening tercile scores use smoothed member counts without the climatology blend; the confirmation scores the blended product.
  • Two multiplicity families are shown: within one method across its targets (✓) and across all methods and targets (✓✓). The confirmation’s selection-aware procedures include the method choice in the evaluation itself.
  • Scores are area-weighted over many correlated cells but tested year by year, so each year counts once.
  • The ordinary CRPS scores the delivered ensemble; the fair CRPS is a diagnostic under a sampling interpretation that DC’s rescaled years and methods tied to the forecast mean or ranks only approximate.
  • Results are national aggregates unless a table says otherwise; a method can rank differently in a region (switch the tables to the regional view).

September initialization · ONDJ and its months

Research benchmark. The published forecasts still use Mean-Variance Scaling (operational). This section compares 12 other rainfall-amount bias-correction methods with it, member by member, for every grid cell and target: a screening of the amount correction alone, then a confirmation through the full probability pipeline that also accounts for how a method is chosen.

Suggested method

The platform suggests a bias-correction method for every target and product from the historical evidence (the confirmation against CHIRPS, counting every method tried) and the independent validation seasons scored since (the shadow and validation runs), by a rule fixed before those seasons are scored. A suggestion is advice for a decision: the published forecast always uses Mean-Variance Scaling until a change is decided. 1 of 10 target–product combinations have a candidate.

The rule
  • Candidate: A method is a candidate only if the confirmation (CHIRPS, outer leave-one-year-out over the training years, full pipeline) finds it better than the operational method with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across every declared method and target, and not worse over the test years. Variants outside the declared family are not candidates.
  • Choice: Among candidates, the method the selection-aware procedure chooses from all training years (training-only information); if that method is not a candidate, the candidate with the best training-period score. Other candidates are listed as alternatives: a confirmation establishes improvement against the operational method, not a ranking among candidates.
  • Validation: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py). A candidate is 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the operational method, and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer seasons it stays a 'candidate'; with enough seasons and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'. Minimum: 3 seasons.

Summary — national aggregate (All Ethiopia)

  • All tested corrections improve national ONDJ rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -0.180; corrected +0.053 to +0.093). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 3 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS (Detrended Quantile Mapping in Dec, Scaled Distribution Mapping in Dec and CDF-transform in Dec).
  • Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Jan) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Jan), and the tercile (RPS) passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Nov, Jan), Power Transformation (Jan) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Jan). Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Empirical Quantile Mapping Jan, Gamma Quantile Mapping ONDJ, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Dec, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling ONDJ and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Jan.

What the evidence supports

  • Published tercile probabilities: no tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling under this validation protocol (several have slightly higher point estimates); the selection-aware procedure is confirmed for none.
  • Rainfall amounts: confirmed against Mean-Variance Scaling (family-wide, full pipeline): Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling for Jan; Gamma Quantile Mapping for Jan. The selection-aware procedure is confirmed for Jan. These comparisons establish improvement against the reference, not that one candidate is better than another.
  • The operational method stays Mean-Variance Scaling until a change is decided by initialization, target and product, and recorded in the docs, on this evidence; confirmed improvements limited to some months may justify a per-target choice.
  • If amounts and probabilities come to use different correction paths, the product metadata must record both methods so that every output can be traced.
  • The same screening and confirmation run for the other cycles with one configuration file each (config/bias_correction/).

Methods

Each method is fitted per grid cell and target from the training years only and applied to each member of the scored year. Methods that keep a “change signal” (DC, DQM, QDM, SDM, CDF-t) were designed for climate change, where a model’s reference period is compared with a future period; here the “future” is the forecast itself: the target year’s ensemble against the model climatology.

How overlapping names were resolved
  • Delta Change appeared twice in the requested list; it is one method.
  • Mean–Variance Scaling is the operational method, with the project’s 0.5–2 ratio limits. Variance Scaling uses the same algebra and the same fallback (ratio 1 where the model spread is below 1 mm) without the limits, so the comparison isolates the limits.
  • Delta Change returns the CHIRPS training years rescaled by the forecast signal (ensemble mean / model climatology): historical scenarios, not corrected members. Applied to each member instead it would be identical to Linear Scaling.
  • Square-root-space MVS (a mean–variance scaling of √x) is distinct from Power Transformation (a·xb with b fitted to the coefficient of variation).
  • The raw model is scored as a baseline, not screened.
Dry totals and tied values

A total at or below 1 mm in the month or season is “dry” (not a dry day). For the quantile-mapping methods (EQM, Gamma QM, DQM, QDM) the dry shares of the model climatology and of CHIRPS are estimated with the equal-year weights; a forecast’s dry members are spread evenly over the model’s dry probability by rank (deterministic stratified tie-breaking, with ties resolved by member index), and a probability within the CHIRPS dry share maps to 0 mm, also after any extrapolation of the upper tail. Without this, tied zeros share one probability and the corrected dry share does not follow CHIRPS. Tests cover repeated zeros, all-dry samples and very few wet values; the dry-month table under Results compares the shares. CDF-t, LOCI and the scaling methods have no occurrence adjustment; SDM uses its own rain-member rule (Switanek et al. 2017).

Steps

  1. 1

    Load

    Per-member totals of every target and year, and CHIRPS for 1993–2024.

    bias_benchmark.py · run_calibration.load_inputs
  2. 2

    Fit

    For each cell and target, the method’s statistics from the training years only, with equal-year weights.

    bias_methods.METHODS[key].fit
  3. 3

    Apply

    Correct every member of the scored year individually (member-wise).

    bias_methods.METHODS[key].apply
  4. 4

    Score

    Ensemble CRPS (and fair CRPS), ensemble-mean errors, spread–error, rank histograms, tercile RPS, dry shares and distribution ratios, per cell; then area-weighted per year.

    bias_benchmark.score_cells · summarise
  5. 5

    Screen

    Each method against Mean-Variance Scaling per target: one-sided sign-flip test on whole years, Holm within the method and across all methods, no harm in 2017–2024.

    bias_benchmark.make_gates
  6. 6

    Confirm

    Every method through the full probability pipeline (blend weight fitted inside the folds), and selection-aware procedures that choose the method each year from training-only scores.

    bias_confirmation.py

CRPS / CRPSSError of the corrected ensemble’s empirical distribution, as delivered, in mm; skill against the CHIRPS training climatology (the training years as an ensemble). Primary amount score.
Fair CRPS / CRPSSThe same under the interpretation that the members are a sample of an underlying distribution; reported as a diagnostic and screened separately. The justification assumes exchangeable members, which DC’s rescaled years and methods tied to the forecast mean or ranks only approximate.Ferro 2014
Ensemble meanBias, MAE, RMSE and correlation over years
Spread–error ratio√(mean ensemble variance·(K+1)/K) / RMSE of the ensemble mean; 1 = spread matches the error, < 1 too narrow
Rank histogram, reliability indexPosition of CHIRPS within the ensemble (10 bins; each rank interval shared among the bins it overlaps); index Σ|fi − 1/10|, 0 = flatDelle Monache et al. 2006
Tercile RPS / RPSS (screening)α = 0.5 smoothed member counts against the training CHIRPS terciles, without the blend: isolates the amount correction
Blended RPSS, Brier skill, reliability (confirmation)The published probability product: counts, smoothing and the climatology blend with its weight fitted inside the folds; category Brier skill for below and above normal; reliability tables
Dry shares and distribution ratiosPooled out-of-fold corrected members (equal-year weights) against CHIRPS of the same years: shares at exactly 0 mm and at ≤ 1 mm; mean, standard deviation, 10th and 90th percentile ratios (area-weighted medians)

Screening statistics for every method, target and score (within-method and family-wide Holm)

Screening rule (docs/36 rule applied as a screen): a method passes for a target and score if, on the leave-one-year-out 1993-2016 per-year scores, its mean improvement over mvs has a one-sided sign-flip p-value below 0.05 after Holm adjustment, and its mean score over 2017-2024 (fits on 1993-2016) is not worse. 'screen_pass': Holm across the 5 targets of one method. 'screen_pass_family': Holm across every method and target of the benchmark for that score. A screening pass is not an operational adoption decision (see the confirmation run).

Where the amount differences come from: cells grouped by their training-year climate

Each cell is grouped by its CHIRPS totals in the fold’s training years only: every year exactly 0 mm; every year ≤ 1 mm (not all 0); some years dry and some wet; never dry. Contributions are area-weighted CRPS differences from Mean-Variance Scaling (mm; negative favours the method) and add up to the national difference. Leave-one-year-out 1993–2016, All Ethiopia.

Confirmation: full pipeline and method selection

The screening isolates the amount correction. The confirmation evaluates what the site publishes: each method’s corrected members go through the full probability pipeline (tercile counts, smoothing and the climatology blend), with every fit and the blend weight inside the cross-validation folds. Two selection-aware procedures then choose a method for each left-out year using only the other training years — SEL-P by the lowest inner blended RPS (probabilities), SEL-A by the lowest inner CRPS (amounts) — so their scores include the effect of choosing among the 14 declared methods. ✓ = better than Mean-Variance Scaling with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 (methods: across all methods and targets; SEL-P/SEL-A: across the targets) and not worse over 2017–2024. MVS ratio-limit study

The operational correction limits the spread ratio r = σobs/σmodel to 0.5–2. This study runs the same screening and confirmation for that correction with wider limits (1/3–3, 1/4–4) and none, all with the same fallback (r = 1 where the model spread is below 1 mm), to see whether the limits are worth changing. ✓ = better than the operational limits with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across the 3 alternatives × 5 targets and not worse over the test years. Run at commit fb7425f.

Confirmed better than the operational limits — published (blended) probabilities: none; rainfall amounts: MVS, ratio limits 1/3-3 (Jan), MVS, ratio limits 1/4-4 (Jan) and Variance Scaling (unbounded) (Jan).
