Figures

Figures show the national aggregate (All Ethiopia) or per-cell maps of the whole country, whatever region is selected for the tables.

Open full size

Interpretation — national aggregate (All Ethiopia)

  1. All tested corrections improve national ONDJ rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -0.180; corrected +0.053 to +0.093). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 3 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS (Detrended Quantile Mapping in Dec, Scaled Distribution Mapping in Dec and CDF-transform in Dec).
  2. Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Jan) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Jan), and the tercile (RPS) passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Nov, Jan), Power Transformation (Jan) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Jan). Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Empirical Quantile Mapping Jan, Gamma Quantile Mapping ONDJ, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Dec, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling ONDJ and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Jan.
  3. Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling is at least as good as Mean-Variance Scaling in the national aggregate for every tested target and period, on amounts and unblended terciles (ONDJ CRPSS +0.080 vs +0.070 in 1993–2016, +0.189 vs +0.178 in 2017–2024). Its ONDJ amount screening pass does not survive the family-wide correction. Members clipped to 0 mm in the months: 4.5%–12.2% with Mean-Variance Scaling, 1.0%–2.9% with this method. This need not hold in each region; see the tables for the ONDJ R3 (Deyr) domain.
  4. The 0.5–2 limits of Mean-Variance Scaling matter most where the raw model is far too narrow (Jan). With the same 1 mm fallback in both, removing the limits is the only difference: there the upper limit is active over 28% of the area and Mean-Variance Scaling stays too narrow (spread–error 0.83), while the unbounded form reaches 1.00.
  5. Empirical Quantile Mapping reproduces the CHIRPS distribution and, with the dry policy, its dry share (totals ≤ 1 mm: Dec 19.0% vs CHIRPS 18.9%; Jan 16.7% vs CHIRPS 16.6%); it passes the screening for Jan, but its ONDJ amount skill is lower than Mean-Variance Scaling (+0.053 vs +0.070). A possible explanation is sampling noise in an empirical quantile function built from 23 CHIRPS values per fold; the results do not isolate it.
  6. Scaled Distribution Mapping follows the published algorithm (Switanek et al. 2017, steps 1–7; checked numerically against an independent implementation of the steps). Where the model is drier than CHIRPS it cannot add rain: in Jan 46% of model members exceed 1 mm against 83% of CHIRPS years, and SDM, by design, keeps the model’s number of rain members, so its corrected dry share is 55% (CHIRPS 17%).
  7. Delta Change has a high ONDJ CRPSS in 1993–2016 (+0.093) but the gain does not pass the screening (Holm p = 0.38), it is lower in 2017–2024 (+0.114 vs +0.178), its ensemble is too wide (spread–error 1.16) and its tercile skill is low. It is the CHIRPS climatology rescaled by the forecast’s mean: historical scenarios, not corrected members.
  8. The methods that use the forecast’s own distribution (Detrended Quantile Mapping, Quantile Delta Mapping, Scaled Distribution Mapping, CDF-transform) score lower on ONDJ terciles (-0.005 to +0.011 vs +0.035) and none passes the season screening. A possible explanation is that the distribution of a single forecast’s 25–51 members is a noisy estimate of the “future” distribution these methods were designed for; the results do not isolate the cause. Where model quantiles are dry, QDM falls back to the CHIRPS quantile (members affected: Dec 32% and Jan 54%), so its quantile changes are only partly preserved.
  9. Linear Scaling and Local Intensity Scaling correct the mean only (LOCI nearly so for totals that are always wet), so the ensemble stays too narrow (spread–error 0.78 and 0.77 for ONDJ).
  10. Dec remains hard: every method has negative amount skill over 2017–2024.
  11. No tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling for the published tercile probabilities under this validation protocol, although several have slightly higher point estimates. Choosing the method each year from training-only scores, the probability procedure (SEL-P) scores ONDJ blended RPSS +0.040 against +0.039, confirmed for none. Amounts: the amount procedure (SEL-A) scores CRPSS +0.093 against +0.070, confirmed for Jan; fixed methods confirmed against the family of all declared methods and targets: Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Jan) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Jan).
  12. The climatology blend narrows the differences. Across the methods, ONDJ RPSS (1993–2016) spans 0.025 after the blend against 0.044 for the unblended screening counts. A better amount correction is trusted more by the blend: in Jan the fitted weight on climatology is 0.60 with Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling against 0.91 with Mean-Variance Scaling.
  13. Choosing by training scores can backfire. For Oct, SEL-A chose Delta Change from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2024 it has a worse mean CRPS (Δ +0.937 mm, 95% interval -0.229 to +2.405 mm; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 4 of 8 years, with the largest losses in 2019 and 2023); for ONDJ, SEL-A chose Delta Change from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2024 it has a worse mean CRPS (Δ +3.217 mm, 95% interval -1.217 to +9.206 mm; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 5 of 8 years, with the largest losses in 2019 and 2023); for Oct, SEL-P chose Gamma Quantile Mapping from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2024 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.003, 95% interval -0.001 to +0.006; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 4 of 8 years, with the largest losses in 2024 and 2019); for Dec, SEL-P chose Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2024 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.001, 95% interval -0.012 to +0.012; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 2 of 8 years, with the largest losses in 2023 and 2021). These choices fail the no-harm rule; where the interval includes 0 they do not establish a significant deterioration. A method that ranks first on the training years is not, on that alone, a replacement.
  14. Where the confirmed amount gains come from (climate groups from each fold’s training years; contributions add up to the national difference from Mean-Variance Scaling): Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling in Jan (Δ CRPS -0.479 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.003 mm (1%; 9% of the area), mixed -0.018 mm (4%; 11% of the area), always wet -0.458 mm (96%; 80% of the area); Gamma Quantile Mapping in Jan (Δ CRPS -0.365 mm): all ≤ 1 mm +0.010 mm (-3%; 9% of the area), mixed +0.003 mm (-1%; 11% of the area), always wet -0.378 mm (104%; 80% of the area).
  15. No cell of All Ethiopia has exactly 0 mm in every training year, for any target, at 0.25° with CHIRPS. The all-zero guard (a separate MVS variant, outside the declared family) therefore never acts and equals Mean-Variance Scaling: the non-zero totals that Mean-Variance Scaling gives where every training year is 0 mm (its spread ratio cannot fall below 0.5) do not arise in these data. The guard remains a documented option; a finite history of zero rainfall does not make rain impossible.
Caveats
  • Screening skill is from 1993–2016 leave-one-year-out (clean) and 2017–2024 (exploratory: these years were seen while the operational method was chosen).
  • Screening tercile scores use smoothed member counts without the climatology blend; the confirmation scores the blended product.
  • Two multiplicity families are shown: within one method across its targets (✓) and across all methods and targets (✓✓). The confirmation’s selection-aware procedures include the method choice in the evaluation itself.
  • Scores are area-weighted over many correlated cells but tested year by year, so each year counts once.
  • The ordinary CRPS scores the delivered ensemble; the fair CRPS is a diagnostic under a sampling interpretation that DC’s rescaled years and methods tied to the forecast mean or ranks only approximate.
  • Results are national aggregates unless a table says otherwise; a method can rank differently in a region (switch the tables to the regional view).

Probability and rainfall-distribution calibration

Can a different probability method improve the tercile probabilities users receive? The published pipeline is MVS-corrected members → smoothed member counts → climatology blend (the incumbent). Phase 1 keeps the amount correction fixed (Pathway A) and replaces only the probability stage: every method starts from the same smoothed, unblended probabilities, except the logistic models, which use declared ensemble predictors (standardized ensemble mean and log spread ratio). Every parameter — the blend weight, the temperature, the Dirichlet map, the logistic coefficients — is fitted only on inner out-of-fold years within each left-out year, and a selection-aware procedure (SEL) chooses the method for each year by inner cross-validation. Later phases add binary-calibration extensions and full rainfall-distribution models (Pathway B). The published forecasts are unchanged.

Definitions kept distinct
  • Pseudocount smoothing pk = (nk + α)/(M + 3α) stabilizes count probabilities; the climatology blend p = (1 − λ)·psmooth + λ·pclim learns how much forecast information to keep. Both are kept as references.
  • Dirichlet calibration (a regularized linear map of the log probabilities, then softmax) is not pseudocount smoothing.
  • Dirichlet uses only the log probabilities; multinomial logistic uses only the ensemble predictors, so they are different models. Ordinal logistic uses the same predictors with ordered cutpoints (below → near → above).
  • All methods are pooled over the grid cells of a target with equal weight per year; a method that cannot be fitted falls back to the incumbent and the fallback is counted.

Shadow forecast · rainfall amounts and ranges (EMOS), not published

Not a published forecast. Since 2026-10-14, each cycle also runs the EMOS distribution model (censored shifted gamma, fitted on the cycle's reference years) and records its median and 10–90% range for every target next to the MVS-corrected ensemble. In Phase 2 the EMOS 10-90% intervals held 76-84% of observed totals where the MVS-corrected ensemble's held 46-76% (80% is calibrated), and EMOS was confirmed better in CRPS for the January-initialized FMAM season and JJAS September. The shadow builds independent evidence season by season before any amount or range product is considered. Each season is scored once its CHIRPS observations exist; any change to what is published is a separate decision after several seasons.

Shadow forecast · rainfall amounts and ranges (EMOS), not published

Not a published forecast. Since 2026-10-14, each cycle also runs the EMOS distribution model (censored shifted gamma, fitted on the cycle's reference years) and records its median and 10–90% range for every target next to the MVS-corrected ensemble. In Phase 2 the EMOS 10-90% intervals held 76-84% of observed totals where the MVS-corrected ensemble's held 46-76% (80% is calibrated), and EMOS was confirmed better in CRPS for the January-initialized FMAM season and JJAS September. The shadow builds independent evidence season by season before any amount or range product is considered. Each season is scored once its CHIRPS observations exist; any change to what is published is a separate decision after several seasons.

Shadow forecast · rainfall amounts and ranges (EMOS), not published

Not a published forecast. Since 2026-10-14, each cycle also runs the EMOS distribution model (censored shifted gamma, fitted on the cycle's reference years) and records its median and 10–90% range for every target next to the MVS-corrected ensemble. In Phase 2 the EMOS 10-90% intervals held 76-84% of observed totals where the MVS-corrected ensemble's held 46-76% (80% is calibrated), and EMOS was confirmed better in CRPS for the January-initialized FMAM season and JJAS September. The shadow builds independent evidence season by season before any amount or range product is considered. Each season is scored once its CHIRPS observations exist; any change to what is published is a separate decision after several seasons.

Shadow forecast · rainfall amounts and ranges (EMOS), not published

Not a published forecast. Since 2026-10-14, each cycle also runs the EMOS distribution model (censored shifted gamma, fitted on the cycle's reference years) and records its median and 10–90% range for every target next to the MVS-corrected ensemble. In Phase 2 the EMOS 10-90% intervals held 76-84% of observed totals where the MVS-corrected ensemble's held 46-76% (80% is calibrated), and EMOS was confirmed better in CRPS for the January-initialized FMAM season and JJAS September. The shadow builds independent evidence season by season before any amount or range product is considered. Each season is scored once its CHIRPS observations exist; any change to what is published is a separate decision after several seasons.

Rainfall climatology and domains

Where does a season's rain matter? Before a forecast domain is chosen, this review computes the observed climatology (seasonal total, annual total and the season's share), compares it with EMI's published long-term maps, and tests every combination of rainfall and annual-share cutoffs. Cutoffs are chosen for what the domain means climatologically, never to improve a forecast score.

Methods & data

In brief

Each cycle starts from the ECMWF SEAS5 seasonal ensemble issued on the 1st of the initialization month. For every 0.25° grid cell in Ethiopia the forecast rainfall is corrected toward the CHIRPS observed mean and variability, then turned into tercile probabilities (below, near or above normal relative to the cycle's CHIRPS reference period). The probabilities are finally blended with climatology using one weight per target, chosen to give the best past scores. Climatology assigns approximately one-third probability to each tercile; the calculations use the observed category frequencies of the training reference period.

Probabilities and amounts are produced separately: the probability skill (RPSS) on this site refers to the blended probabilities, and the rainfall amount skill (CRPSS) to the amount-corrected ensemble.

The raw benchmark is the uncorrected model: raw ECMWF members counted against each cell's CHIRPS tercile limits, with no correction, smoothing or blend. For May-initialized JJAS over 2017–2025 it scores RPSS −0.44, far below climatology, which is why calibration is needed.

CHIRPS v2.0 vs v3.0 (why and what changed, 11 October 2026)

CHIRPS v3.0 (Funk et al. 2026) replaced v2.0 for calibration and verification. Over Ethiopia, 1993–2025, v3.0 is about 15% wetter (consistent with its gauge-undercatch correction) while each season's share of annual rainfall and the ranking of years agree closely, so tercile limits move up. The same method was refitted on v3.0: the decision gates give the same outcome, and skill is similar overall. Each version is scored against its own observations.

Workflow (eight scripted stages)
  1. 1

    Download

    ECMWF SEAS5 (system 51) daily accumulated precipitation from the Copernicus CDS for the initialization month, 1993 to the forecast year.

    download_seasonal_forecasts_daily_c3s.py
  2. 2

    Inspect

    Inventory every year: initialization, lead times, member counts and accumulation increments (GRIB packing tolerance 0.2 mm).

    inspect_inputs.py
  3. 3

    Prepare

    De-accumulate to daily totals, sum the season and each month; CHIRPS on the same dates.

    prepare_seasonal.py · run_monthly.py
  4. 4

    Regrid

    Each 1° model cell is copied into its 4×4 block of 0.25° CHIRPS cells (no interpolation).

    regrid_seasonal.py
  5. 5

    Calibrate

    Per-cell amount correction, smoothed tercile counts and one climatology-blend weight per target.

    final_shared_blend.py
  6. 6

    Evaluate

    Nested cross-validation 1993–2016; exploratory fixed-fit scores for later years; whole-year significance tests.

    local_blend.py · decision_gates.py
  7. 7

    Deliver

    Maps, summaries and an offline gallery; forecasts frozen with SHA-256 hashes before observations are used.

    run_operational.py · build_season_products.py
  8. 8

    Verify

    Official CHIRPS v3.0 monthly files, checked against the archive where they overlap, scored per month and season.

    prepare_verification_2026.py · verify_frozen_2026.py

Every stage is a script in scripts/; documents in docs/ record each step, issue and decision (runbook: docs/38; per-season guides: docs/40).

Equations
  1. Amount correction per cell, equal weight per year: x̂ = max(0, μobs + r·(x − μmodel)), r = clip(σobs/σmodel, 0.5, 2)
  2. Tercile probabilities from the corrected members against CHIRPS tercile limits, smoothed: (n + 0.5)/(M + 1.5)
  3. Climatology blend: pfinal = (1 − λ)·pmodel + λ·pclimatology, with one λ per target fitted on leave-one-year-out RPS.
    pclimatology is, for each grid cell, the observed frequency of each tercile in the training reference years (about one-third each; it differs slightly because of sample size, category limits and ties).
  4. Skill score: RPSS = 1 − RPSforecast / RPSclimatology; RPSS +0.05 means a 5% lower ranked probability score than climatology. CRPSS is the same for rainfall amounts.
Method and references

Rainfall amounts are corrected cell by cell with mean–variance scaling (also called simple bias adjustment or variance scaling; Teutschbein & Seibert 2012; Torralba et al. 2017; Manzanas et al. 2019): each member is shifted to the CHIRPS mean and its anomaly rescaled by the ratio of CHIRPS to model standard deviation (equations above). It corrects the mean and spread, not the shape of the distribution; it is not quantile mapping. The model mean and spread are pooled over all members and years, with equal weight per year (25 members to 2016, 51 from 2017); training years 1993–2025.

Probabilities are the share of corrected members in each CHIRPS tercile (ensemble relative frequency; Wilks 2019), smoothed so no category is 0 or 1, then blended with climatology. Weighting a model against climatology follows Rajagopalan et al. (2002) and Robertson et al. (2004); here one weight per target is fitted by minimising the ranked probability score of leave-one-year-out probabilities.

Scores: ranked probability score (Epstein 1969) and continuous ranked probability score (Hersbach 2000), as skill scores against climatology. Forecasts: ECMWF SEAS5 (Johnson et al. 2019); observations: CHIRPS v3.0 (Funk et al. 2026), v2.0 before 11 October 2026 (Funk et al. 2015).

Choices of this project, not taken from a single paper: the 0.5–2 limits on the spread ratio, mean-only correction where the model spread is below 1 mm, clipping at 0 mm (its weakness in dry months, issue I-08), equal weighting of years, the count smoothing and one blend weight shared by all cells. A square-root-space amount correction passed the gate for amounts and is recommended for the next cycle (docs/36). Details: docs/46. DOIs checked on Crossref, 11 October 2026.

How the method was chosen

A change is adopted only if it improves the cross-validated 1993–2016 scores (Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 over the five JJAS targets) and does not worsen 2017–2025. Also evaluated and not adopted: regularized Dirichlet recalibration and per-cell or regime-specific blend weights.

Calibration parameters are fitted mostly on 25-member hindcasts and applied to 51-member forecasts. In 2017–2025 the 51-member forecasts scored about the same as, or slightly better than, 25-member subsets, so the transfer did not degrade scores in the years tested; this does not show it is neutral in every year or region. The corrected ensemble is under-dispersive (spread smaller than error), which the climatology blend partly offsets. Monthly and seasonal outlooks are calibrated separately: for JJAS 2026 over all Ethiopia the corrected monthly means sum to 432 mm against 430 mm for the season (+1.7 mm).

Quality control
  • Every forecast file is inventoried; re-downloaded years were bit-identical, confirming SEAS5 system 51.
  • Small negative daily increments (≤ 0.15 mm) are GRIB packing rounding; tolerated up to 0.2 mm and clipped, and the seasonal sum is checked.
  • CHIRPS sea cells (223) are always missing; no partial season enters any fit.
  • Verification observations are compared with the archive in the overlap year (tolerance 0.0001 mm/day) before use.
Limitations
  • Few evaluation years and single verification seasons give wide uncertainty; regional and monthly results are noisy.
  • The later evaluation years were inspected during method development; the cleanest evidence is the cross-validated 1993–2016 score.
  • The 0.25° maps repeat 1° model information; they add no dynamical detail.
  • All cycles are research reconstructions produced after their initialization dates, not official EMI or ICPAC forecasts.
Reproduce 
git clone https://github.com/YonSci/calibrated_seasonal_rainfall.git
python -m venv .venv && .venv\Scripts\activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
set CALIBRATION_CYCLE=config\cycles\sep_2026_ondj.json
python scripts\run_operational.py --config config\cycles\sep_2026_ondj.json --workflow all
python scripts\build_site.py

Raw ECMWF and CHIRPS data are not stored in the repository. Step-by-step guides: docs/40; project status: docs/36.
